subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: Should an unavailable native Codex approval relay fall back to `before_tool_call` policy, and if so, which explicitly classified relay failures are safe to downgrade?
rationale: The current patch changes an authorization failure boundary; source inspection can identify the overbroad catch, but only maintainers can confirm the intended permanent security policy.

options.title: Narrow fallback and refresh
options.body: Implement descriptor refresh or re-registration, allow fallback only for explicit relay-unavailable states, and retain fail-closed handling for unknown errors.

options.title: Preserve fail-closed behavior
options.body: Remove the app-server fallback and solve restart recovery entirely through relay lifecycle and descriptor regeneration.

options.title: Accept broad policy fallback
options.body: Keep the broader fallback only with explicit security-owner approval and live evidence that both native and normal policy paths enforce equivalent decisions.

recommendation.title: Narrow fallback and refresh
recommendation.body: Implement descriptor refresh or re-registration, allow fallback only for explicit relay-unavailable states, and retain fail-closed handling for unknown errors.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision depends on the generation and registry invariants established in Kaspre's native-relay lifecycle work.
